claims.claim: Convergence detector still false-converges on polite agreement: round>=2 + empty disagreed_with_peer + agreed_with_peer covering peer claim_ids returns 'converged'; stalled fires only when ALL agents emit zero claims; the ledger veto only blocks on has_unverified_in_round / has_lineage_flag_in_round, neither of which fires when one well-formed (but possibly irrelevant) citation lands. Peer A2 reaches the same conclusion via a different framing.

Required evidence_path is necessary-but-insufficient: _verify_one_citation returns status='verified' as soon as _resolve_path succeeds and _extract_snippet returns lines in range; claim text is never compared to snippet. Peer A3 strengthens this with a point I missed in round 1 — PositionEvidence.content_snippet is defined in the schema but verify_position only walks claims and disagreed_with_peer evidence_path values, so the schema's most directly falsifiable field is dead code.

Single highest-priority improvement (reaffirmed, sharpened by peer A1+A3): upgrade the verifier from 'file resolves + line range in bounds' to '(claim, snippet) semantic-support check' AND start consuming PositionEvidence.content_snippet (compare agent-supplied snippet to actually-resolved snippet, flag drift). Emit two new ledger statuses: 'citation_does_not_support_claim' and 'snippet_drift'. This closes b1/b2/A2/A3 in one move because detect_convergence already refuses to fire 'converged' when has_unverified_in_round is true. Without this, peer's A1 obligation loop ships obligations like 'address this verified-but-irrelevant citation' which are not actionable signal.

Direct disagreement with peer A1 on ordering, not on merit. Peer A1 is correct that verifier_ledger entries are written to state/disk but never injected into the next-round prompt (deliberate.py:386-419 confirms prompt embeds only peer-latest and own-prior). But shipping the obligation loop BEFORE fixing semantic verification means agents are told to 'resolve' obligations attached to status='verified' rows that already satisfy the existence-only contract. The obligation loop is the right SECOND step: (1) make ledger statuses semantically meaningful, then (2) pipe unresolved/non-supporting entries into prompts as required obligations. Reversing the order ships motion without signal.

Held from round 1, peer did not address: build_deliberation_workflow has no task_family parameter despite the module docstring claiming chassis parity with duet (Plan #31 TaskFamily registry). Domains wanting deliberation variants with extra Position fields must fork. Structural asymmetry — but lower leverage than b8/b9 because no shipped caller currently needs a non-generic deliberation schema.

Held from round 1, peer did not raise: synthesis defaults to claude-code/opus, which is exactly DEFAULT_AGENT_PAIR's agent_b model. In a default run the 'tiebreaker' shares model family with one participant, distorting residual_disagreements. This is independent of b8/A1 and remains uniquely my finding.

Held from round 1: _detect_silent_rename keys on first 80 chars of claim text. Symmetric leading-edit evasion not addressed by the trailing-edit comment. Lower leverage than b8/b9 because rename detection is a defense-in-depth layer that only matters once the convergence-detector itself stops trusting self-reported agreement.

Revised after peer A5: I partially concede. Per-round position prompts remain bounded (peer-latest + own-prior, deliberate.py:386-409), so 'context bloat' is not the per-round failure — my round-1 framing stands. BUT peer A5 correctly identifies a one-shot bloat point at synthesis: synthesize_findings_node serializes the full position_history. So at max_rounds>5 the failure shape is: (a) per-round ledger growth in verifier_ledger.json (verifier:559-606 appends, never compacts), (b) terminal synthesis-prompt bloat once history is 5+ rounds, (c) drift because agents never see cumulative verifier state. All three are real; budget exhaustion is not the first failure because max_budget is trace-cumulative.

Held from round 1, converges with peer A6: duet (gated cycle) + deliberation (peer debate) is missing a third pattern — N peers + non-peer arbiter with terminate authority. Synthesis half-implements this but does not gate. Peer A6 frames it as 'judge-guided audit/repair' routing obligations back; same shape, different name. Lower leverage than b8/b9 because no current caller needs it.

disagreed_with_peer.my_counterclaim: Peer A1 is correct on the gap (verifier writes ledger entries that never reach next-round prompts, deliberate.py:386-419) but wrong on priority ranking. Piping obligations into prompts BEFORE upgrading what the ledger means produces feedback that says 'address this verified-but-existence-only citation' — agents have nothing actionable to do because the ledger row already says verified=true. Correct order: (1) b8 semantic-support verification so ledger statuses carry signal, (2) A1 obligation loop to route that signal back to agents. Reversing the order ships plumbing without payload.

Partial disagreement: peer A5 is right that budget is not the first failure (max_budget is trace-cumulative, call_contracts.py:136-145) and right that terminal synthesis serializes full position_history (deliberate.py:621-638). But A5 understates per-round ledger growth — verifier_ledger.json appends every citation entry every round and never compacts (verifier.py:559-606), so at max_rounds>5 ledger I/O and resolver hot-path cost grow O(rounds*claims_per_round). First failures, in order: (a) per-round ledger growth, (b) terminal synthesis bloat, (c) drift from agents lacking cumulative verifier state. Drift is third, not first.

open_questions: Should the semantic-support check be deterministic (lexical/embedding overlap floor) or LLM-as-judge? Deterministic is cheaper and auditable; LLM-as-judge catches paraphrase but adds a per-claim provider call to every round.

If b8 lands first, does the obligation loop (peer A1) become trivial to add — just inject ledger entries with status in {'citation_does_not_support_claim','snippet_drift','unresolved'} into the next-round prompt as a required-obligations section?
Does verifier_ledger.json get replayed on checkpointer resume, or does initial_state={verifier_ledger:[]} (deliberate.py:847) reset it? Affects whether ledger growth is bounded per-run.
reviewer_summary: Revised ranking after peer round 1 (residual disagreement with peer is explicit on A1 ordering and A5 first-failure shape, NOT papered over): (1) b8 semantic-support verification + consume PositionEvidence.content_snippet — strictly foundational because without it every downstream fix (convergence detector, obligation loop, rename detection) operates on a 'verified=file exists' substrate that carries no signal. (2) Peer A1 obligation loop — correct mechanism, must ship AFTER b8 so the obligations it routes carry meaning. (3) b4 synthesis-judge neutrality — independent fix peer didn't raise, distorts the only durable productive_disagreement artifact. (4) b3 deliberation-TaskFamily parity — structural docstring lie. (5) b5 80-char rename-prefix brittleness. (6) b6/A5 max_rounds>5 failure shape — per-round ledger growth first, terminal synthesis bloat second, drift third. (7) A4/b7 three-agent + arbiter pattern — future work. Single highest-priority improvement: b8. One-paragraph justification: the chassis's load-bearing groundedness contract is the required evidence_path field, but the verifier today only checks that the path resolves and that line range is in bounds — it never checks that the snippet supports the claim, and it never reads the schema's required content_snippet field. As a result, status='verified' carries no semantic signal, convergence_detector's ledger veto (deliberate.py:300-307) fires only on narrow has_unverified_in_round / has_lineage_flag_in_round cases, and the polite-agent false-convergence path stays open. Upgrading the verifier to emit 'citation_does_not_support_claim' and 'snippet_drift' statuses, and including content_snippet in the comparison, simultaneously hardens convergence detection (b1/A2), makes evidence_path actually falsifiable (b2/A3), and gives peer A1's proposed obligation loop something real to route. No other single change touches as many shipped failure modes.
